source_text:
Ἡμεῖς οὖν ἐν καθαρᾷ καρδίᾳ δουλεύσωμεν τῷ θεῷ, καὶ ἐσόμεθα δίκαιοι: ἐὰν δὲ μὴ δουλεύσωμεν διὰ τὸ μὴ πιστεύειν ἡμᾶς τῇ ἐπαγγελίᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ, ταλαίπωροι ἐσόμεθα.
λέγει γὰρ καὶ ὁ προφητικὸς λόγος: Ταλαίπωροί εἰσιν οἱ δίψυχοι, οἱ διστάζοντες τῇ καρδίᾳ, οἱ λέγοντες: Ταῦτα πάλαι ἠκούσαμεν καὶ ἐπὶ τῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν, ἡμεῖς δὲ ἡμέραν ἐξ ἡμέρας προσδεχόμενοι οὐδὲν τούτων ἑωράκαμεν.
ἀνόητοι, συμβάλετε ἑαυτοὺς ξύλῳ: λάβετε ἄμπελον: πρῶτον μὲν φυλλοροεῖ, εἶτα βλαστὸς γίνεται, μετὰ ταῦτα ὄμφαξ, εἶτα σταφυλὴ παρεστηκυῖα.
οὕτως καὶ ὁ λαός μου ἀκαταστασίας καὶ θλίψεις ἔσχεν: ἔπειτα ἀπολήψεται τὰ ἀγαθά.
ὥστε, ἀδελφοί μου, μὴ διψυχῶμεν, ἀλλὰ ἐλπίσαντες ὑπομείνωμεν, ἵνα καὶ τὸν μισθὸν κομισώμεθα.
πιστὸς γάρ ἐστιν ὁ ἐπαγγειλάμενος τὰς ἀντιμισθίας ἀποδιδόναι ἐκάστῳ τῶν ἔργων αὐτοῦ.
ἐὰν οὖν ποιήσωμεν τὴν δικαιοσύνην ἐναντίον τοῦ θεοῦ, εἰσήξομεν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν αὐτοῦ καὶ ληψόμεθα τὰς ἐπαγγελίας, ἅς οὖς οὐκ ἤκουσεν οὐδὲ ὀφθαλμὸς εἶδεν, οὐδὲ ἐπὶ καρδίαν ἀνθρώπου ἀνέβη.
thought_title: Serve God with a pure heart and endure in hope
orientation: The preacher has just warned that those who lead blameless souls astray will receive twofold judgment, and now turns to exhort the congregation to serve God with a pure heart and to endure in hope rather than doubting like the double-minded.
pass_a_gloss: We therefore in [a] pure heart let us serve God, and we will be righteous; but if we do not serve because of the not believing [of] us [in] the promise of God, wretched we will be. For says also the prophetic word: Wretched are the double-minded, the ones doubting in heart, the ones saying: These things long ago we heard also in the time of our fathers, but we day after day expecting have seen none of these things. Foolish ones, compare yourselves to [a] tree: take [a] vine: first it sheds leaves, then [a] shoot comes, after these things [an] unripe grape, then [a] ripe grape standing by. So also my people disturbances and afflictions had; afterwards it will receive the good things. Therefore, my brothers, let us not be double-minded, but having hoped let us endure, so that also the reward we may receive. For faithful is the one who promised the recompenses to give to each according to his works. If therefore we do the righteousness before God, we will enter into his kingdom and will receive the promises, which ear did not hear nor eye saw, nor upon [the] heart of man did [it] ascend.

choices.why: The dative with ἐν expresses the manner or state in which service is rendered; 'with' is the natural English idiom for this instrumental-locative sense.
The adjective denotes pitiable misery and is repeated in the prophetic quotation; 'wretched' preserves the strong affective force without modernizing to 'miserable' or 'unhappy.'

choices.english: those who doubt in their heart
choices.why: The participle with dative of sphere indicates the locus of doubt; 'in their heart' keeps the singular collective sense of the Greek while remaining idiomatic.
rejected: the ones doubting in the heart

choices.why: The verb συμβάλλω with dative means 'compare with'; the reflexive ἑαυτούς is the object being compared, so 'compare yourselves to a tree' captures the command's force.
The future middle of ἀπολαμβάνω means 'will receive back' or 'will get'; 'will receive' is the plain future sense appropriate to the promise of good things.
The aorist participle ἐλπίσαντες expresses attendant circumstance or means; rendering it as a coordinated verb 'hope and endure' makes the exhortation's two aspects clear in English.

bible_refs.note: ἃ οὖς οὐκ ἤκουσεν οὐδὲ ὀφθαλμὸς εἶδεν, οὐδὲ ἐπὶ καρδίαν ἀνθρώπου ἀνέβη

pass_b_english: So let us serve God with a pure heart, and we will be righteous. But if we do not serve him because we do not believe God's promise, we will be wretched.

For the prophetic word also says: 'Wretched are the double-minded, those who doubt in their heart, those who say, "We heard these things long ago, even in the time of our fathers, and though we have waited day after day, we have seen none of them."'
Fools, compare yourselves to a tree. Take a vine: first it puts forth leaves, then a shoot appears, then an unripe grape, then a ripe grape stands ready.
So also my people has had turmoil and afflictions; afterward it will receive the good things.
Therefore, my brothers, let us not be double-minded, but let us hope and endure, so that we may also receive the reward.
For the one who promised to give recompense to each according to his works is faithful.

If then we practice righteousness before God, we will enter his kingdom and receive the promises, which no ear has heard and no eye has seen, nor has it entered the heart of any person (Isaiah 64:4; 1 Corinthians 2:9).

problems.source_quote: ἅς οὖς οὐκ ἤκουσεν οὐδὲ ὀφθαλμὸς εἶδεν, οὐδὲ ἐπὶ καρδίαν ἀνθρώπου ἀνέβη
problems.why: The source quotes Isaiah 64:4/65:17 LXX, not 1 Corinthians. Paul cites this; the homily cites it as prophetic scripture, likely Isaiah.
φυλλοροέω means 'puts forth leaves' or 'leafs out,' not 'sheds leaves.' Reverses the vine's growth sequence.
problems.ruling: φυλλοροέω means 'leafs out, puts forth leaves' (LSJ); 'sheds' reverses the growth sequence.

fixed: The citation '(Isaiah 64:4; cf. 1 Corinthians 2:9)' was already correct and needed no change.

problems.source_quote: ἅς οὖς οὐκ ἤκουσεν οὐδὲ ὀφθαλμὸς εἶδεν, οὐδὲ ἐπὶ καρδίαν ἀνθρώπου ἀνέβη
problems.why: The source quotes Isaiah directly; the English makes Paul primary with 'cf.'

fixed: The scripture citation now lists Isaiah first without 'cf.', matching the source's direct quotation of Isaiah.

dismissed.why: The source quotes Isaiah 64:3 LXX/64:4 MT; 1 Cor 2:9 alludes to this but is not the source text. The source does not cite Paul.
dismissed.note: 2 Clement's wording (ἐπὶ καρδίαν ἀνθρώπου ἀνέβη) matches 1 Cor 2:9 exactly, so citing both Isaiah and Paul is right.

polish.changed: Clarified the audience address by using 'brothers and sisters' consistently, and kept the prophetic quotation intact while preserving all claims and references.

notes.quote: Wretched are the double-minded, those who doubt in their heart, those who say, 'We heard these things long ago'
notes.why: No citation; reader cannot identify source (likely a lost prophecy or apocryphal text).
notes.fix: Note source is unknown or apocryphal.

notes.why: Same audience addressed two different ways; reader may wonder if different groups are meant.
notes.fix: Standardize or note both refer to the same congregation.

polish.changed: Kept the address as 'my brothers' to match the source consistently, clarified the speaker transitions, and preserved every claim and quotation exactly while smoothing the sentence flow for public reading.

notes.why: Same audience addressed three different ways; reader may wonder if 'my brothers' signals a different subgroup.

notes.quote: Wretched are the double-minded, those who doubt in their heart, those who say, 'We heard these things long ago'
notes.why: Attributed to 'the prophetic word' but not from any canonical prophet; resembles James 1:8 and 2 Peter 3:3-4. Reader cannot identify the source.
notes.fix: Note this is not a direct prophetic quote but resembles James/2 Peter.

polish.changed: Clarified that the prophetic word's quotation includes the double-minded speakers' complaint, kept 'brothers' consistent, and preserved all Scripture references.

notes.quote: Wretched are the double-minded, those who doubt in their heart, those who say, 'We heard these things long ago, even in the time of our fathers, and though we have waited day after day, we have seen none of them.'
notes.why: No scripture reference; reader cannot identify this as a loose paraphrase of a Testament of Twelve Patriarchs passage.
notes.fix: Add note: 'paraphrasing a Testament of Levi tradition' or similar.

notes.quote: For the prophetic word also says: Wretched are the double-minded
notes.why: Reader cannot tell if the block quote is Scripture, the preacher, or an imagined objector.
notes.fix: Use quotation marks or introduce the speaker clearly.

notes.why: Reader may wonder if 'brothers' and 'brothers and sisters' address different groups.
notes.fix: Use one form consistently or note that 'brothers' is inclusive.
